answer.evidence: radon/visitors.py:257-260: visit_Assert does `self.complexity += not self.no_assert`. It adds a bool, so it adds 1 only when no_assert is False. That matches the request, but it's implicit, and an explicit `if not self.no_assert:` would be clearer. no_assert defaults to False in ComplexityVisitor.__init__ (line 157/165). It's propagated to nested visitors at lines 279 and 313 (`no_assert=self.no_assert`), and that propagation needs a test. radon/complexity.py is where the flag enters from the caller, so I'd check there that it's passed through to the visitor (about 12 min). Tests in radon/tests/test_complexity_utils.py and test_ipynb.py only set no_assert=False. There's no test of the True case or of nested functions and classes, so I'd add one. radon/raw.py and radon/metrics.py don't reference assert handling, so they get only a brief check. I weighted the minutes toward visitors.py because that's where the logic is.
